- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias or add early correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” rule to cap forecast growth for 3–5 days.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model often fails to reverse trend; add a “sentiment reversal” heuristic to trigger mean reversion in forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent mean or add lag correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if history shows high volatility or sentiment divergence, reduce forecast smoothness and increase sensitivity to recent sentiment shifts.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often misreads direction; use sentiment median as a proxy for trend direction, not absolute value.
